seven_q.Q0_posture: Analytical and constructive; the document assumes the isomorphism is valid and explores its implications with rigorous mathematical and theological reasoning
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record (ISO-012) mapping the mathematical structure of a Hermitian sign operator with eigenvalues ±1 to the theological concept of moral orientation, specifically within Reformed soteriology
seven_q.Q2_domain: Intersection of quantum mechanics (operator algebra), Reformed theology (soteriology), and mathematical philosophy (structural isomorphism)
seven_q.Q3_claim: The mathematical structure of a binary sign operator σ with [σ, U_self] = 0 (invariance under self-evolution) maps onto the Reformed theological claim that self-effort cannot change moral orientation (total depravity), and that an external non-commuting operator V_grace is required for sign flip (grace alone)
seven_q.Q4_support: Rigorous mathematical derivation from quantum mechanics (constants of motion, commutation relations), scriptural evidence (Romans 3, Ephesians 2, Matthew 12), and theological tradition (Westminster Confession, Reformed orthodoxy)
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Depends on the validity of Reformed theological anthropology (binary moral status), the mathematical framework of Hermitian operators and commutation, and the acceptance of structural isomorphism as a valid method
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Rules out Pelagianism as mathematically impossible; predicts behavioral improvement without sign change; constrains soteriology to require external grace; provides a mathematical language for discussing grace vs works
seven_q.Q7_kill: The mapping fails if moral orientation is not binary (e.g., Catholic venial/mortal sin distinction, Eastern Orthodox theosis as continuous process, or secular multidimensional moral frameworks); also fails if a genuine case of self-salvation is demonstrated

graph_summary.one_sentence: ISO-012 establishes a structural isomorphism between the quantum mechanical sign operator (with eigenvalues ±1 and commutation invariance under self-evolution) and the Reformed theological claim that moral orientation is binary, self-effort cannot change it, and external grace is required for salvation.
